title: States Weekly: October 7, 2026
gist: CSIS's India States Weekly roundup for October 7, 2026 lists state-level policy moves: Bihar's green hydrogen policy targeting 100,000 tons/year by 2031, Karnataka's textile policy seeking $2.07 billion of investment and 500,000 jobs, Gujarat's GCC guidelines, and a wave of deregulation and decriminalization bills in Jammu and Kashmir and Odisha.

insights.claim: Bihar's Green Hydrogen Policy 2026 targets 100,000 tons of green hydrogen annually by 2031, backed by 1 GW of electrolyzer capacity, 2.5 GW of renewables and $1.67 billion (INR 16,000 crore) of investment.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Adds to Indian electrolyzer and renewable demand pipelines from subnational policy.
insights.locator: Bihar issues the Bihar Green Hydrogen Policy 2026

insights.claim: Jammu and Kashmir released a Compressed Biogas Policy 2026 offering financial incentives, subsidized land and time-bound approvals, plus an Electric Vehicle Policy 2026-2032 setting a six-year e-mobility roadmap.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Incremental subnational incentives for biogas and EV adoption in India.

insights.claim: Uttarakhand's electricity regulator approved an additional surcharge of INR 0.67 (about $0.0069) per unit on open access power consumers from October 1, 2026 to March 31, 2027.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Raises costs for industrial buyers procuring power via open access, including renewable PPAs.

insights.claim: Gujarat will offer up to a 50 percent motor vehicle tax concession on new vehicle registrations backed by a certificate of authorized scrapping of old vehicles.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Scrappage incentives can support new auto sales in Gujarat.

insights.claim: Karnataka's Textile and Apparel Policy 2026-2031 aims to attract $2.07 billion (INR 20,000 crore) of domestic and foreign investment and create 500,000 jobs, focusing on Northeastern Karnataka and Tier 2 and 3 cities.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Indian states are competing for textile supply-chain relocation investment.
insights.locator: Karnataka announces a Textile and Apparel Policy

insights.claim: Odisha's Jan Vishwas Bill 2026 amends 62 provisions across 16 state acts, decriminalizes 35 minor offenses and eases 27 licensing requirements; Odisha also repealed its professional tax on salaried employees.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Reflects a broader Indian push to cut compliance burdens, improving ease of doing business.
insights.locator: Odisha passes the Odisha Jan Vishwas Bill 2026

insights.claim: Jammu and Kashmir's Ease of Doing Business Bill 2026 provides time-bound approvals, deemed clearances, fewer no-objection certificates and limits on routine inspections of new enterprises.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Regulatory easing may support investment in a historically conflict-affected region.
insights.locator: Jammu and Kashmir passes the Jammu and Kashmir Ease

insights.claim: Gujarat released operational guidelines for its Global Capability Centers Policy 2025-2030, providing a framework for recognizing, setting up and expanding GCCs.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: States are competing for multinational GCC offshoring, a key Indian services growth engine.

insights.claim: Odisha replaced slab-based apartment stamp duty of 3 to 5 percent with a uniform 5 percent rate and a flat INR 50,000 duty on transfer of common areas to owners' associations.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Raises effective transaction cost for lower-value apartments while simplifying registration.

insights.claim: Bihar removed VAT on aviation turbine fuel at airports under the modified UDAN 6.0 regional connectivity scheme, which spans FY2026-27 to FY2035-36.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Lower fuel taxes improve regional airline economics in India.

insights.claim: Madhya Pradesh approved a 20 percent horizontal reservation for former Agniveers in uniformed services recruitment including police constables and forest guards.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: States are absorbing short-term army recruits, easing a political pain point of the Agnipath scheme.

insights.claim: Andhra Pradesh approved a Social Media Influencers policy that empanels content creators to publicize government schemes.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Indian state governments are becoming paying customers of the creator economy.
